title: The Empty Package Index
description: The apt lists were wiped from the image; run apt update and record the nginx candidate version.
scenario: This image was built with `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` to keep it small — which means apt can no longer look anything up: even `apt list nginx` finds nothing. Refresh the index with apt update, then use apt-cache policy to find out which nginx version the archives would install, and record it in /home/intern/pkg-report.txt as nginx-candidate=<version>. This lab's container has network access.
symptoms: `apt list nginx` reports no matches although the package obviously exists
/var/lib/apt/lists is empty — no package index files at all
apt-cache policy shows no Candidate for nginx
mission: Run apt update to rebuild the index, then record the nginx candidate version in /home/intern/pkg-report.txt.

hints.title: What update really does
hints.content: apt-get update downloads fresh index files into /var/lib/apt/lists/. Install anything you like afterwards — but without this step apt is blind.

hints.title: Who would install what
hints.content: `apt-cache policy nginx` prints Installed: (none) and Candidate: <version> — the version a fresh install would get right now.

hints.title: Capture the version
hints.content: `apt-cache policy nginx | grep 'Candidate:' | awk '{print $2}'` isolates the version string for your report line.

acceptance_criteria.description: package index files exist again under /var/lib/apt/lists
report records the nginx candidate version
